title: Technology Sector Update for 02/27/2018: FB,AAPL,XRX
text:

Declines for technology stocks were starting to accelerate, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 dropping almost 0.6% in value Tuesday while the Philadelphia semiconductor index still was posting a less than 0.1% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Facebook ( FB ) was down 1.2 % in recent trading Tuesday to $182.60 a share after the social networking company and CEO Mark Zuckerberg late Monday reaching a $35 million agreement to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging the company concealed internal worries over the company's growth prospects prior to its May 2012 initial public offering of stock. Citing a federal court filing, Reuters reported the Arkansas Teacher Retirement System along with the Fresno County (Calif.) Employees Retirement Association charged the company hid from the public worries over projected slow growth on mobile devices potentially reducing its revenue while quietly warning investment bankers and analysts to cut their forecasts.
In other sector news:
+ Apple ( AAPL ) continued to hold on to a slim gain Tuesday afternoon, easing from a nearly 1% rise to a new record high of $180.48 a share earlier in the day, following reports the tech giant is planning to release three new smartphones late this year. One of the phones will be Apple's largest ever, according to Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the matter. Another smartphone will produce a handset the same size as the current iPhone X while the third device will be a less expensive version of the latest iPhone model.
- Xerox ( XRX ) fell Tuesday after activist shareholder Darwin Deason disclosed in a regulatory filing he was planning to nominate and run an alternative director slate at its upcoming annual meeting. Xerox closed nominations for the next shareholder meeting on Dec. 11, 2017, but Deason contends New York securities law allows investors in any company dominciled in the state to sidestep that deadline following a material change at the company - which include its proposed merger with Fujifilm, Deason said. Together with Carl Icahn, who also has expressed his opposition to the upcoming deal, the two investors own a combined 15.2% of Xerox's outstanding stock.
